entries.note: The repercussions forecast explicitly says 'likely.' The embedded claim about the market drop is separately checkable.
Neither 'win the AI race' nor the degree of doubt has a shared evidentiary threshold here.

entries.test: Public model comparisons, company financial results, Nvidia business performance, semiconductor-policy outcomes, model costs and reliability evaluations, and research funding patterns through publication would establish whether the listed predictions substantially materialized.
entries.note: This is a retrospective endorsement of the entire preceding list. 'Basically' allows approximate fulfillment, not omission of major predictions.
The causal framing is explicit, but 'fantasies,' 'massively blundered,' 'precarious,' and 'marginal' supply no shared test for this combined claim.
The principal commitment is a judgment about what US policy should have been.

entries.test: The continued operation of Google, Microsoft and Amazon and their demonstrated capacity to supply US AI needs, including classified deployments, would test the claim.
entries.note: Marcus asserts their staying power and capacity outright; the normalization makes that assertion conditional on two competitors failing. 'Presumably' qualifies the subsidiary remark about Chinese models.

entries.test: If an open-source AI ban is enacted, public evidence of continued substantial distribution and use of open LLMs through prohibited channels or countries without bans would test his prediction.
entries.note: The following sentence makes the substantive prediction explicit: open source would continue to thrive even if illegal. The normalization substitutes an uncertain prediction about outlawing succeeding for this claim about continued availability.

entries.test: Following adoption of a US regulatory moat, public price, innovation, and business-impact evidence would test whether it slowed progress, raised prices, and benefited OpenAI and Anthropic at the expense of hundreds of thousands of other companies.
entries.note: This is a firm prediction contingent on a possible policy, not an inaccessible counterfactual.
'A great gift to humanity' expresses the value Marcus assigns to the proposed policy package.
